annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 117
annotation.summary_en: EU Regulation 2017/746 sets rules for placing on the market and putting into service in vitro diagnostic medical devices, replacing Directive 98/79/EC. It establishes four risk classes, notified body conformity assessment, performance evaluation and studies, UDI traceability, the Eudamed database, vigilance and market surveillance. It is not AI-specific.
key_provisions_or_claims: Four risk classes (A-D) with notified body involvement for B, C and D
General safety and performance requirements, CE marking and harmonised standards or common specifications
Manufacturers must have quality management, risk management, post-market surveillance and financial coverage for liability
Unique Device Identification and Eudamed database for transparency and traceability
Vigilance, incident reporting and market surveillance by national competent authorities, coordinated via the MDCG
